newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close up on technicals, China talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close up on technicals, China talk.

text.p: A technical bounce plus talk China overnight bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"There is talk China bought 50,000 tonnes of beans for November shipment," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Traders acknowledged the China talk but pointed to the very oversold status in the soybean complex as central to the gains.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November soybeans closed at 18.323 points, below the 20 level which generally is considered a very oversold area.
"It's just technical. We were due for a bounce," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Gains were limited by technical selling near the $6.95 level, the traders said.
"It (Nov) couldn't penetrate the $6.95 area, yesterday's high and today's high, but we'll see what happens tomorrow," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Also gains were muted by active harvesting in the U.S. Midwest under near ideal weather conditions.
Soybeans closed two to five cents per bushel higher, with November up four at $6.92-1/2.

"If the weather outlook is good they will probably beat it down again tomorrow," Bruce said. "There is no reason for bulls to step up and buy. At best bulls will wait for the market to go sideways at best."

The rally was trimmed by a light number in Tuesday's USDA weekly export inspections report. USDA said 10.480 million bushels of soybeans were inspected for export during the week ended October 10, below the 15.5 million inspected the same week a year ago. The weekly tally was below trade expectations for 12 million to 16 million bushels.

Key players included Cargill Inc which bought three million bushels of November, The Chicago Corp which bought 2.5 million January and LIT America which bought two million bushels of January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 61,000 contracts, down from 79,271 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 November $6.75 puts at 1-1/2 cents, Continental Grain bought 450 November $7.00 calls at 3-3/4 to four cents, E.D. and F. Man International bought 450 November $7.25 puts at 34 and Cargill Investor Services bought 500 January $7.75 calls at 2-1/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 38,000, down from 50,559 Monday.
